Train AUC 0.9189, accuracy 0.921. Performance sources (train): all units replaced by least-squares linear fits gives AUC 0.8336 (an L2 logistic regression refit on all 71 inputs gets 0.8433); restoring usage_response alone gives 0.9189 (all the gain); its parts alone: usage hinge 0.8803, heavy-use hinge 0.8870, service-calls gate 0.8731. The international-plan, voicemail and state units are exact switches/offsets and restore nothing. Rare-category switches: state:46 -1.89 logit (80 rows, empirical log-odds offset -0.91); state:39 -1.23 (82, -0.93); state:47 +1.10 (72, +0.92); state:5 -1.09 (78, -0.51); state:45 -0.97 (91, -0.85); state:26 +0.81 (75, +0.50); state:49 -0.69 (122, -0.32); state:0 -0.68 (56, -0.76); state:10 -0.63 (60, -0.22); state:41 +0.25 mean, range -3.85..+0.43 (66, -0.04: it switches off the 1406 day-charge hinge, so heavy users lose up to 3.85).

sentences.text: This part combines a usage score, built from daytime, evening and night-time minutes and the voice-mail plan, with calls to customer service, not as a simple sum.

Customer-service calls add only from about 3 calls upwards, for most customers slowly at first, then faster, but for some customers without a voice-mail plan they add nothing until a point, then steadily: going from 0 to 4 calls takes a typical customer from about 1% to about 15%.

Through it, daytime minutes add to the chance only above about 187 minutes for customers without a voice-mail plan, in an uneven way: for a typical customer, going from 0 to 271 minutes takes it from about 1% to about 11%.

parts.original_hypothesis: Root: logit P(churn) = -1.96 + linear_backbone (identity_lin) + usage_response (identity_usage) + 1.68*6711 (intl_plan_switch) - 1.40*582 (vmail_state41_unit) + state_offsets (-0.26*2067 - 0.10*5821 + 0.02*12726 + 0.13*13164 - 0.12*13420 + 0.03*5667), purely additive in the logit; the sigmoid is the only coupling. 35 inputs are unconnected (international minutes, night charge, evening charge and calls, day calls, area codes 408/415 and 29 state indicators) and have zero effect. Train AUC 0.9189, accuracy 0.921. Performance sources (train): all units replaced by least-squares linear fits gives AUC 0.8336 (an L2 logistic regression refit on all 71 inputs gets 0.8433); restoring usage_response alone gives 0.9189 (all the gain); its parts alone: usage hinge 0.8803, heavy-use hinge 0.8870, service-calls gate 0.8731. The international-plan, voicemail and state units are exact switches/offsets and restore nothing. Rare-category switches: state:46 -1.89 logit (80 rows, empirical log-odds offset -0.91); state:39 -1.23 (82, -0.93); state:47 +1.10 (72, +0.92); state:5 -1.09 (78, -0.51); state:45 -0.97 (91, -0.85); state:26 +0.81 (75, +0.50); state:49 -0.69 (122, -0.32); state:0 -0.68 (56, -0.76); state:10 -0.63 (60, -0.22); state:41 +0.25 mean, range -3.85..+0.43 (66, -0.04: it switches off the 1406 day-charge hinge, so heavy users lose up to 3.85).

parts.original_hypothesis: Composition on usage_hinge: identity_usage = 2.57*879 + 3.06*10552 + 2.88*4344 enters the logit with weight 1. 10552 = relu(-0.64 + 1.17*relu(-0.16 + 1.08*879)) is a second, steeper hinge that opens once 879 exceeds 0.65 (about 240 day minutes at median other use; active for 12% of customers), so the usage effect accelerates. 4344 = relu(-0.38 + 0.75 calls - 3.24*879) is a service-calls gate: shut for 0-2 calls, open from 3 calls, and closed again by usage (at 3 calls once 879 > 0.14, at 5 calls once 879 > 0.49). Hypothesis: usage and service calls interact non-additively: service calls raise churn only for low-usage customers (or voicemail-plan customers, for whom usage is off), heavy users get the usage hinges instead. Evidence (train): usage logit (879+10552) by day minutes 0.14 (<200), 0.58 (200-220), 1.08 (220-240), 2.02 (240-260), 3.43 (260-280), 6.37 (>=280); churn 0.10/0.06/0.14/0.26/0.46/0.67 vs model 0.09/0.09/0.17/0.30/0.49/0.69. Without a voicemail plan churn reaches 0.84 above 280 minutes (model 0.86), with a plan 0.04 (model 0.09). Gate logit at 0-7 calls: 0/0/0/0.80/2.11/3.59/5.30/7.08 (1.25/2.90/4.55/6.20 at 3-6 calls when usage is off, 0.10/0.50/1.05/2.01 when it is on). Churn by calls 0.115/0.110/0.110/0.106/0.437/0.571/0.679/0.545 vs model 0.116/0.111/0.109/0.150/0.319/0.598/0.849/0.940: the gate opens one call too early (3 calls: +0.80 logit, empirical churn unchanged) and is over-confident from 6 calls (39 customers). Mean ablation of all three terms AUC 0.6557 (the largest drop: full 0.9189); gate alone 0.8202, heavy-use hinge alone 0.9093; linear replacement 0.8336 (R2 0.53/0.29/0.53); restoring usage_response alone onto the all-linear model recovers 0.9189 (all-linear 0.8336), i.e. all of the gain.
